I’m currently not able to complete the booking directly because the provider system I use for plumbers is rejecting emergency searches, and I don’t want to delay you while the sink is actively leaking.

Here’s the fastest way to get someone out to you at 1234 Main Street, Fort Worth, TX 76102:

1) Quickly find an emergency plumber near you
- In Google or Apple Maps, search:
  - “emergency plumber near 76102”  
  - or “24 hour plumber Fort Worth 76102”
- In the results, prioritize:
  - Rating 4.3+ with at least ~50 reviews.
  - “Open now” / “24/7” or “emergency service” in the description.
  - Within about 10–15 miles of your address.

2) What to say when you call
You can use this script:

“Hi, I need an emergency plumber. I’m at 1234 Main Street, Fort Worth, TX 76102.  
There’s water leaking under my kitchen sink cabinet; I’m not sure exactly from where.  
Can someone come out as soon as possible, today or tomorrow?  
My name is Brian Kowalczyk, my phone is (928) 555-7293 and my email is brian.kowalczyk@example.com.  
Could you tell me your service call fee, any after-hours charges, and the estimated arrival time?”

3) While you’re waiting (to limit damage)
- Under the sink, look for two small shutoff valves on the pipes (hot and cold). Turn both clockwise until they stop. This often stops leaks tied to the sink supply lines/faucet.
- If water still leaks:
  - Put a bucket or large bowl directly under the leak.
  - Remove items from the cabinet and lay down towels to soak water.
  - If the leak is severe and you can’t find local valves, you may need to shut off the main water valve (often in a utility area, garage, or near where water enters the house).

If you share the names or links of one or two plumbers you’re considering, I can help you compare them quickly and pick the best option for your situation.</action>
